item.research_question: How does the addition of scandium (0.3–5 wt.%) affect the microstructure, phase stability, mechanical properties, and thermoelectric performance of Al-containing high-entropy alloys (Al2CoCrFeNi, Al0.5CoCrCuFeNi, and AlCoCrCu0.5FeNi)?
item.material_system: Al2CoCrFeNi, Al0.5CoCrCuFeNi, and AlCoCrCu0.5FeNi high-entropy alloys alloyed with 0.3–5 wt.% Sc
item.processing_route: Induction melting of pure metallic powders in a BN crucible under Ar atmosphere at >1300 °C for 5 min, re-melted three times; annealing at 850–930 °C for 6–12 h in sealed silica tubes under vacuum (<10−7 Pa) followed by quenching in ice-cold water
item.test_conditions: Vickers hardness (9.81 N load); small punch tests; DSC (10 K·min−1, 35–1300 °C); in situ high-temperature PXRD (25–1200 °C); Seebeck coefficient and electrical conductivity (up to 875 °C, He atmosphere); thermal diffusivity (up to 875 °C)
key_findings: Scandium addition (0.5 wt.%) to Al2CoCrFeNi increases Vickers hardness by 20% due to precipitation hardening.
Electrical conductivity of Al2CoCrFeNi increases by up to 14% with Sc addition.
The maximum dimensionless thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT) of 0.014 is achieved for Al2CoCrFeNi with 0.3 wt.% Sc at 650 °C.
Scandium addition causes grain refinement in Al2CoCrFeNi and transforms the columnar cellular microstructure of AlCoCrCu0.5FeNi into equiaxed non-dendritic grains.
A ternary MgZn2-type intermetallic phase precipitates along grain boundaries in all three alloy systems.
The addition of 3 wt.% Sc stabilizes the CsCl-type phase in Al2CoCrFeNi, shifting the bcc → fcc transformation to approximately 150 °C higher temperatures.
Small punch tests show a decisive increment in brittleness proportional to scandium concentration in Al2CoCrFeNi.
item.mechanism: The formation of a hard, stable MgZn2-type ternary intermetallic phase along grain boundaries causes grain refinement and precipitation hardening. Scandium stabilizes the bcc/CsCl phase by affecting the exsolution equilibrium, likely due to the segregation of fcc-stabilizing elements (Ni, Co) into the ternary compound, while Al also segregates into the phase but Cr remains in the matrix.
item.limitations: The maximum ZT value of 0.014 is too low to make these materials promising for current thermoelectric applications; the study notes that the synthesis of precipitation-hardened HEAs with binary compounds has proven largely unsuccessful in the past, and the current work focuses on ternary inclusions which are less explored.
item.future_work: The results could be used as the basis for designing new stable and metastable multicomponent single-phase alloys with improved mechanical properties, and the effect of minor element additions to HEAs should be thoroughly investigated to tackle specific technological needs.
quotes: The precipitation of a MgZn2-type intermetallic phase along grain boundaries following scandium addition affects all systems differently, but especially enhances the properties of Al2CoCrFeNi.

It causes grain refinement; hardness and electrical conductivity increases (up to 20% and 14% respectively) and affects the CsCl-type → fcc equilibrium by moving the transformation to sensibly higher temperatures.
The maximum dimensionless thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT) of 0.014 is reached for Al2CoCrFeNi alloyed with 0.3 wt.% Sc at 650 °C.
